Subject: Acme DPA redline (subprocessors & breach timeline)

Hi Neha,

Thanks for sending the DPA template. Attached is Acme's redline (high level items only):

- Subprocessors: we need a contractual commitment that Redwood will provide 30 days' notice for new subprocessors that may have access to Personal Data, and an opt-out right for high-risk subprocessors.
- Breach notification: our legal team requires initial written notice within 24 hours of discovery for any incident involving Personal Data, followed by daily updates until root cause is determined.
- Incident cooperation: we want explicit commitments for forensic evidence preservation and assistance for regulatory reporting.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on each? We prefer to execute via DocuSign once we have agreed language.

Attached: Acme_Redline_DPA_v2.docx (redline)

Best,

Hi Lindsey / Neha — thanks for the redline. I reviewed Acme's edits and propose the following compromise language and rationale:

1) Subprocessors
- Redwood will maintain and publish a subprocessor registry and provide notice of any additions at least 30 days prior to onboarding.
- For subprocessors that we reasonably determine will process sensitive Personal Data or have elevated access, Redwood will notify the customer and provide reasonable mitigation options. We cannot agree to an opt-out that prevents use of core infrastructure subprocessors because that would break delivery of service. Instead, we can include a right to require additional security assessments and, for extraordinary cases, refuse the subprocessor where feasible.

2) Breach notification and cooperation
- Initial notification: Redwood will provide an initial written notification to the customer's designated security contact "without undue delay and, in any event, within forty-eight (48) hours of discovery" for incidents materially affecting Personal Data.
- Ongoing updates: Redwood will provide reasonably requested updates at least every 24–72 hours as the investigation progresses (frequency to be determined by severity).
- Forensic cooperation: Redwood will preserve evidence and cooperate reasonably in regulatory reporting; Redwood's assistance includes access to timelines, affected data categories, and remediation steps, subject to investigation integrity and legal privileges.

Rationale: a 48-hour initial window is a compromise between Acme's preference for 24 hours and Redwood's operational requirement to verify and avoid sending inaccurate notices. We can commit to faster initial notification for high-confidence detections and provide next-day detailed updates.

I've attached a clean DPA with the suggested language. If that fits, we can produce a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Clean_exec.pdf

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-05-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme DPA redline (subprocessors & breach timeline)

Marissa — thanks for the thoughtful response and the suggested compromise. A few follow-ups from Acme Legal:

- 48 hours initial notification is acceptable for many incidents; we would still like a clear escalation path for incidents deemed high-risk by Acme (e.g., exposure of customer PII) that requires immediate notification to our Incident Response lead (we will provide a 24/7 contact).
- Updates cadence: can we specify "daily updates while the incident is open" rather than a range? Consistency helps our regulators.
- Subprocessor opt-out: we understand the delivery constraints. Please include that Redwood will provide a 30-day notice and publish reseller/infra subprocessors in the registry; for any new subprocessor with access to plaintext Personal Data, Redwood will obtain customer approval if reasonable alternatives exist.

Also, please confirm whether Redwood can share a current SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; that will speed Acme's internal risk sign-off.

Once we have that language, we can finalize and sign via DocuSign.

Best,
Lindsey

Lindsey — good points. Quick confirmation from our side on the items you flagged:

- 24/7 escalation: yes — please send the Incident Response lead contact and we'll include it in the DocuSign annex so the security team can use it for urgent notifications.
- Updates cadence: Redwood can commit to daily updates while an incident remains open. We'll include a sentence that says "Redwood will provide daily updates to the customer's designated security contact until the incident is remediated or otherwise closed."
- Subprocessors: Redwood will publish a subprocessor registry and provide 30 days' notice for new subprocessors. For subprocessors with access to plaintext Personal Data, Redwood will (i) notify the customer, (ii) provide reasonable mitigation options, and (iii) where feasible and reasonable alternatives exist, seek customer approval prior to onboarding.
- SOC 2: we can share the SOC 2 Type II under NDA. I'll have Priyom follow up with a secure link to the report.
